papers.title_in_file: Is data-efficient learning feasible with quantum models?
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, method, results, discussion, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: Simulation study of quantum kernel methods on relabeled classical tabular datasets, with a data-generation tool and a spectral-bias generalization metric.

assertions.value: The authors report that on fully classical datasets, quantum kernel methods can require fewer training examples than classical kernels to reach comparable error.
quotes: we show that on fully classical datasets, QKMs can require fewer training examples than classical kernels to reach comparable error
To our knowledge this is the first empirical evidence that this is in fact possible.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study on semi-artificial relabeled data.
assertions.reader_inference: The datasets are relabeled to favor the quantum kernel, so this shows existence of such datasets, not general quantum advantage.

assertions.value: The authors state that the datasets keep the original features and replace only the labels, and that the three tabular datasets are reduced to 8 features by PCA.
quotes: Since only labels are being altered but features remain the same, we call these datasets semi-artificial in this work.
We apply Principal Component Analysis (PCA), reducing the datasets to 8 key features.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of setup and scope.

assertions.value: The authors report that predicted loss from the spectral-bias generalization metric stays consistent with empirical behavior in the quantum kernel setting.
quotes: The overall trends of predicted loss from Eq. (7) remain consistent with empirical behavior.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that their smoothness analysis is not conclusive on its own and that the chosen metrics do not fully capture the observed functional artifacts.
quotes: Overall, while not conclusive on their own, these results demonstrate the usefulness of our artificial labeling tool.
the chosen metrics do not fully capture them
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its limits.

papers.title_in_file: High-Performance Computing with Quantum Processing Units
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, method, results, discussion, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: Architecture paper analyzing loose and tight integration of quantum processing units into HPC systems and proposing new performance metrics.

assertions.value: The authors identify two pathways for integrating QPUs into HPC systems, tight integration that assumes infrastructure bottlenecks can be overcome and loose integration that assumes they cannot.
quotes: We identify two integration pathways that are differentiated by infrastructure constraints on the QPU and the use cases expected for the HPC system.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own framing of its analysis.

assertions.value: The authors state that a quantum interconnect can enlarge the set of accessible register states but that it is unclear whether it would give a net benefit, because entanglement between nodes exposes the system to a more serious fault model with correlated errors.
quotes: it remains unclear if the interconnect would provide a net benefit
assertions.certainty_reason: Author reasoning without experiment in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that existing metrics for conventional computing do not capture all aspects of QPU behavior and suggest new features to track.
quotes: Existing metrics for conventional computing do not capture all aspects of the QPU behavior
assertions.certainty_reason: Author claim without measurement.

papers.title_in_file: Preparing for Post-Quantum Critical Infrastructure: Assessments of Quantum Computing Vulnerabilities of National Critical Functions
papers.partial_detail: Summary, key findings, contents; the remainder of the report (per-NCF assessments) not read in detail
papers.what_it_is: RAND Homeland Security Operational Analysis Center report assessing 55 U.S. national critical functions for quantum cryptographic vulnerability and prioritizing assistance.

assertions.value: The authors report that, after assessing 55 national critical functions, they rated six as high priority for assistance, 15 as medium priority and 34 as low priority.
quotes: we rated six of the NCFs as a high priority for assistance, 15 as medium priority for assistance, and 34 as low priority for assistance
creating individual, high-level assessments of each of the 55 NCFs
assertions.certainty_reason: Analyst ratings from one assessment, a judgment-based result.

assertions.value: The authors state that three NCFs were identified as critical enablers of the PQC migration.
quotes: Three NCFs were identified as critical enablers of the PQC migration:
assertions.certainty_reason: Analyst judgment in one report.

assertions.value: The authors state that practical challenges in executing catch-and-exploit campaigns mean very few NCFs likely need to urgently address catch-and-exploit vulnerabilities, although many NCFs will exhibit them.
quotes: Practical challenges in executing catch-and-exploit campaigns mean that very few NCFs likely need to urgently address catch-and-exploit vulnerabilities, although many NCFs will exhibit them.
assertions.certainty_reason: Author assessment without measurement.

assertions.value: The authors state that many factors related to the PQC migration are still unknown or uncertain, and that it is uncertain when a sufficiently capable quantum computer will be created.
quotes: Many factors related to the PQC migration are still unknown or uncertain.
it is uncertain when a sufficiently capable quantum computer will be created
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope and limits.

papers.title_in_file: HybridQ: A Hybrid Simulator for Quantum Circuits
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, method, results, discussion, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: NASA Ames software paper describing HybridQ, an extensible Python and C++ simulator of quantum circuits combining state vector, tensor contraction and Clifford expansion.

assertions.value: The authors state that HybridQ integrates multiple simulation techniques under one framework and supports CPUs, GPUs and TPUs.
quotes: HybridQ also allows simulation on multiple backends, including CPUs, GPUs, and TPUs, both on single nodes or on heterogeneous HPC clusters.
Fully integrates multiple techniques under the same common framework:
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors describing their own software.

assertions.value: The authors report that on one 4-core machine HybridQ substantially outperforms QuTiP (version 4.7) after around 7 qubits when applying a depolarizing channel to each qubit.
quotes: We find after around 7 qubits, HybridQ substrantially outperforms QuTiP.
All tests are performed on the same machine with a 2.5 GHz Quad-Core Intel Core i7 chip, and 16GB RAM
assertions.certainty_reason: Single benchmark by the tool's own authors on one machine.

assertions.value: The authors state that state-vector parallelization on multiple nodes is planned for the next release, so it is not available in the described version.
quotes: state-vector parallelization on multiple nodes is planned on the next HybridQ release
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope.

papers.title_in_file: Mind the O~: asymptotically better, but still impractical, quantum distributed algorithms
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, method, results, discussion, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: Theory paper giving Quantum CONGEST-CLIQUE algorithms for Steiner trees and directed minimum spanning trees, with explicit constant and log factors.

assertions.value: The authors report two algorithms in the Quantum CONGEST-CLIQUE model, for an approximately optimal Steiner tree and an exact directed minimum spanning tree, that achieve lower asymptotic round and message complexity than any known algorithms in the classical CONGEST-CLIQUE model.
quotes: The algorithms thus achieve a lower asymptotic round and message complexity than any known algorithms in the classical CONGEST-CLIQUE model.
assertions.certainty_reason: Asymptotic upper bounds proved in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors report that after tracing constants and logarithmic factors, their algorithms and related ones need improvement to be practical, because the asymptotic speedups only help for very large values of n.
quotes: The analysis shows that some improvements are needed to render both our and existing related quantum and classical algorithms practical, as their asymptotic speedups only help for very large values of n.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own analysis of its algorithms.

assertions.value: The authors state that Steiner tree and minimum spanning tree problems cannot benefit from quantum communication in the standard CONGEST (non-clique) model, citing Elkin et al. 2012.
quotes: these problems cannot see quantum speedups in the CONGEST (non-clique) setting as shown in (Elkin et al., 2012)
assertions.certainty_reason: Result attributed to other work.

papers.title_in_file: Is Quantum Optimization Ready? An Effort Towards Neural Network Compression using Adiabatic Quantum Computing
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, method, results, discussion, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: Exploratory paper formulating joint pruning-quantization of CNNs as QUBO and solving it on quantum annealing devices from D-Wave and Fujitsu.

assertions.value: The authors report that they demonstrate adiabatic quantum computing achieving effective compression of practical DNN models, and that it outperforms genetic algorithms and reinforcement learning in time efficiency and in finding global optima.
quotes: we demonstrate that AQC can achieve effective compression of practical DNN models
not only outperforms classical algorithms like genetic algorithms and reinforcement learning in terms of time efficiency but also excels at identifying global optima
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is on small models chosen to fit the annealers.

assertions.value: The authors state that they selected models of sufficiently small problem size because of qubit count and connectivity limits, namely LeNet-5, ResNet-9 and VGG-16.
quotes: which are LeNet-5, ResNet-9, and VGG-16.
The different annealing technologies impose constraints on the neural network architectures due to the limited number of nodes and their connectivity.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum optimization can potentially provide quality compression solutions for practical small-scale neural networks, and that their experiments remain limited by current annealing technology constraints, including qubit count and connectivity.
quotes: We find that quantum optimization can potentially provide quality compression solutions for practical small-scale neural networks.
our experiments remain limited by current constraints of annealing technologies, including qubit count and connectivity
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its limits.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum and Classical Machine Learning in Decentralized Finance: Comparative Evidence from Multi-Asset Backtesting of Automated Market Makers
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, method, results, discussion, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: Backtesting comparison of 10 classical, quantum and hybrid models on cryptocurrency trading, from Omnis Labs.

assertions.value: The authors report that hybrid quantum models reach 11.2% average return and 1.42 average Sharpe ratio, while classical ML models show 9.8% average return and 1.47 average Sharpe ratio.
quotes: hybrid quantum models achieve superior overall performance with 11.2% average return and 1.42 average Sharpe ratio, while classical ML models show 9.8% average return and 1.47 average Sharpe ratio
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical backtest from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The hybrid average return is higher but its average Sharpe ratio is lower than classical, so the abstract's word superior rests on return only.

assertions.value: The authors report that all pure quantum models (VQE, QNN, QSVM) achieved poor returns of 3.00% to 4.77% and low Sharpe ratios of 0.79 to 0.87.
quotes: All pure quantum models (VQE, QNN, QSVM) achieve poor returns (3.00% - 4.77%) and low Sharpe ratios (0.79 - 0.87)
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical backtest from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that Random Forest and Gradient Boosting achieved returns of 12.31% to 13.16% with Sharpe ratios of 1.68, against the best hybrid return of 13.99% with Sharpe ratio 1.76.
quotes: Random Forest and Gradient Boosting achieve excellent returns (12.31% - 13.16%) with high Sharpe ratios (1.68)
QASA Sequence model achieves the highest return (13.99%) with the best Sharpe ratio (1.76)
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical backtest from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the study is based only on cryptocurrency data, so results may not apply to other financial markets, and that the backtests used three asset pairs.
quotes: Study based only on cryptocurrency data; results may not apply to other financial markets.
three major crypto asset pairs (BTCUSDC, ETHUSDC, USDCUSDT)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of its limits.
